passage:
A student found her mother's old report card. The grades were not all high, which surprised her.
Her mother laughed and said she had struggled with math. The student had always thought adults were finished products who had somehow become capable.
The report card made her mother's past visible. It showed effort, weakness, and growth.
That night, the student felt less ashamed about her own difficult subjects.
Old documents can reduce distance between generations. A report card is not only a record of grades. Years later, it can become evidence that people change.
